 import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Sector': [
        'Public Health Expansion', 'Public Health Expansion', 'Public Health Expansion',
        'Primary Education Reforms', 'Primary Education Reforms', 'Primary Education Reforms',
        'Agricultural Subsidies', 'Agricultural Subsidies', 'Agricultural Subsidies',

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

    x='Sector',
    y='FundingUtilizationRate',
    color='Region',

The chart is divided into eleven distinct sectors listed along the horizontal axis, including Public Health Expansion, Primary Education Reforms, Agricultural Subsidies, Transport Infrastructure, Clean Water Projects, Sanitation Programs, Rural Clinics, Teacher Training, Irrigation Systems, Water Treatment Plants, and Waste Management. The vertical axis represents the funding utilization rate as a percentage, ranging from 76% to 92%.

Each sector displays grouped box plots in three colors: blue for the National region, red for the Rural region, and green for the Urban region. The box plots provide a visual summary of the distribution of funding utilization rates, highlighting the median, interquartile range, and potential outliers.

For Public Health Expansion, the National region shows a median utilization rate around 88%, with values ranging from approximately 85% to 90%. Primary Education Reforms in the National region have a slightly higher median near 90%, with a range from about 89% to 92%. Agricultural Subsidies, represented in the Rural region, display a median near 90%, spanning from 88% to 92%. Transport Infrastructure in the National region shows a median around 89%, with a wider spread from 86% to 91%.

Clean Water Projects in the National region have a lower median utilization rate, around 81%, and range from 79% to 84%. Sanitation Programs in the Rural region show an even lower median around 79%, with values between 76% and 82%. Rural Clinics in the Rural region exhibit a high median utilization rate near 90%, ranging from 88% to 91%. Teacher Training in the National region has a median rate of about 91%, with values between 89% and 93%.

Irrigation Systems in the Rural region show a median near 89%, ranging from 87% to 90%. Water Treatment Plants in the National region have a median around 82%, with values between 81% and 83%. Lastly, Waste Management in the Urban region displays a median utilization rate around 80%, ranging from approximately 78% to 82%. Each box plot also includes whiskers that extend to indicate variability outside the upper and lower quartiles, and some show slight outliers. The chart effectively conveys the variation in funding utilization rates across different sectors and regions during the specified timeframe.

s = Path("chart.py").read_text()
start = s.index("data = {")
end = s.index("\nfig = px.box(")
s = s[:start] + 'df = pd.read_csv("table.csv")\n' + s[end:]
s = s.replace("    y='FundingUtilizationRate',\n", "")
s = s.replace("fig.update_layout(", """# Use the exact five-number summaries supplied in the source table.
for trace in fig.data:
    rows = df[df['Region'] == trace.name]
    trace.update(
        x=rows['Sector'].tolist(),
        y=None,
        q1=rows['Q1'].tolist(),
        median=rows['Median'].tolist(),
        q3=rows['Q3'].tolist(),
        lowerfence=rows['Min'].tolist(),
        upperfence=rows['Max'].tolist()
    )

fig.update_layout(""")
s = s.replace("yaxis_title='Development Sector'", "yaxis_title='Funding Utilization Rate (%)'")
Path("chart.py").write_text(s)
exec(compile(s, "chart.py", "exec"))

assert fig.layout.yaxis.title.text == "Funding Utilization Rate (%)"
for trace in fig.data:
    rows = df_table[df_table.Region == trace.name]
    for attr, col in [('q1','Q1'),('median','Median'),('q3','Q3'),
                      ('lowerfence','Min'),('upperfence','Max')]:
        assert list(getattr(trace, attr)) == rows[col].tolist()
print("Verified all box statistics and the vertical-axis title against table.csv.")
print("Title:", fig.layout.title.text)
print("Dimensions:", fig.layout.width, fig.layout.height)
print("Colors:", [(t.name, t.marker.color) for t in fig.data])
